evidence: Method: built a criterion -> public-requirement map for all 2 gate, 36 Functional, 5 Polish and 5 Visual criteria against instruction.md, hireops_rules.md, integration.md and app_context.md, then checked each graded detail for a source in the public text or a professional default, and compared suspicious details with the golden's own choices. RESULT: no criterion demands an exact label, exact route, selector, field name, layout or a stage/permission rule that only the reference implements; every protocol says 'Do not require routes, selectors, field names, layouts or exact wording' (functional/prompt.md:15) and app_context.md:33-34 forbids assuming reference routes. Sign-in in the gates is the known false positive (skill Known false positives; Internal Quality Checks row 27 annotation) and the brief does require sign-in anyway (instruction.md:17, rules section 1). Traced examples that ARE public: 401 for anonymous (hro_anonymous <- rules.md:21 'A caller with no valid session reads and writes nothing: 401'); not found for another application's conversation (hro_candidate_private <- rules.md:22-23); focus on the card's controls after a refused move (hro_refused_put_back <- rules.md:84-85); per-person unread incl. Lena's 1 (seed reads USR-CAN3/APP-301 read_count 2 of 3 messages, third from USR-REC3 -> 1 unread; rules.md:151-154); seen not counted for observer (hro_seen <- rules.md:164-166); 30-message pages and remaining count (rules.md:144-147); undo blocked by reorder but not by note (hro_undo_conflict/hro_undo_restores <- rules.md:96-100); per-person drafts surviving sign-out and hidden from Mei, note drafts kept per person/browser (hro_pol_session_resume/hro_pol_failed_send <- instruction.md:7, rules.md:106,170-175); one-stage, bulk board order, Interview places, manager late stages (rules.md:47-100); Activity newest-first, filter, rejection reason, refused adds nothing (rules.md:110-113); candidate wording table and forbidden fields (rules.md:179-194); 15-second live updates preserving typing/focus/open card/scroll (instruction.md:5, rules.md:117-123). Visual Likert rows only use generic craft anchors and the visual prompt says 'Layout, labels and styles are the implementer's choice' (visual/prompt.md:14). Residual P3 instances where a criterion's wording leans on a display or logging choice that the public text does not explicitly state (each mirrors the golden, each is arguably a professional default, none is a demonstrated false-fail): (1) hro_job_open (functional/judge.toml:29, weight 0.5) passes only if the job 'appears with those values' (title, team, hiring manager, interview places) - the public text requires the job to HAVE these (rules.md:27-29) but never requires staff screens to display the team or hiring manager; the golden displays 'Recruiter X · Hiring manager Y' (board.js:366), 'title · team' (board.js:353) and 'Interview (n of N places)' (board.js:327). (2) hro_add_candidate (judge.toml:38, weight 0.5) requires the card to appear 'with the entered name and email'; rules.md:31 requires the email be entered, not displayed; golden shows it on the card meta (board.js:251) and details (board.js:130). (3) hro_reject_reason (judge.toml:83) requires the rejected-from stage to be 'available to staff'; rules.md:50 says only that the workspace 'remembers' it (in practice also visible via the Activity line's 'what changed' and the reopen target, so low risk); golden shows 'Rejected from X: reason' (board.js:~255). (4) hro_activity (judge.toml:263) and protocol A (prompt.md:49) say 'each card of every single and multi-card move' has its line; rules.md:96 treats a multi-card move as one 'move' and rules.md:110-111 requires only 'a readable line' per move; the golden logs one row per application (index.js:195-197 log(jobId, appId,...)). A combined line naming every card and its stages should satisfy the wording, but a literal judge could read it as one line per card. I found no criterion that grades exact text, routes, colours, coordinate bases, keyboard conventions beyond Enter/Shift+Enter (which are public, rules.md:138-139) or a hidden rule. No configured judge run on a conforming alternative app exists (raw-evidence-index.json scope), so whether the GLM judge actually false-fails these wordings is unmeasured.
counterexample: Conforming alternative that could be false-failed: a HireOps build that stores and enforces each job's team, hiring manager and interview places (Ingrid can work J1's late stages, Interview refuses a third card) but whose staff board shows only the job title in a picker and candidate names on cards (email only in an edit form), and writes one Activity line per bulk action ('Rafael Costa moved Y, W and X from Applied to Screen'). A literal judge could give hro_job_open 0 ('does not appear with team/hiring manager/places'), hro_add_candidate 0 ('email not shown') and hro_activity 0 ('no separate line for each card'), although no public sentence requires those displays or per-card lines. Conversely, a broken app cannot exploit these wordings; they only risk false-fails.
suggested_fix: Either publish the expectation (e.g. in hireops_rules.md: the board shows each job's team, hiring manager and interview places, cards show the candidate's email, a rejected card shows its reason and the stage it came from, and Activity names every card of a multi-card move) or relax hro_job_open/hro_add_candidate/hro_reject_reason to 'visible wherever the app shows job/card details, or evidenced by behaviour' and state in hro_activity that one line naming every card and its from/to stages satisfies a multi-card move.
